messages:
maya: heads-up: small surge of tiny-gang evictions in ap-southeast1 at ~03:05 UTC, looks correlated with node heartbeat drops :rotating_light:
ravi: saw that. nodes gpu-node-apse1-{50..55} reported 'heartbeat lost' then NotReady, kubelet events show conntrack table full errors
infra-bot: alert: conntrack_full on ap-southeast1-nat-2 (pool=1) at 03:03 UTC. affected nodes: gpu-node-apse1-50..55
devon: snippet from kubelet logs:
```
Mar 03 03:03:02 kubelet[1234]: E0303 03:03:02 cni.go:215] failed to set up network for pod "gpu-train-9": conntrack: table full
Mar 03 03:03:03 kubelet[1234]: W0303 03:03:03 kubelet_node_status.go:298] Node became not ready: NetworkUnavailable
```
maya: ah, nat pool size was reduced yesterday as a cost test, we've seen conntrack bumps before when nat endpoints shrink
ravi: mitigation: scaled nat pool back to 2 -> 4, restarted CNI on affected nodes, and bumped warmpool-min from 2 -> 6 for 30m to absorb reschedules. also temporarily raised scheduler's evictionThreshold to 5m
ops-bot: action created: NET-7721 revert-nat-test-and-collect-conntrack-dumps (assigned to netops)
devon: metrics: pod_evictions spiked 3 -> 38 in 4m, now down to 7 after fixes. recommending postmortem: ensure nat-pool CI prevents pool=1 for gpu clusters and add monitor for conntrack_usage > 80%
maya: job owners affected: 12011, 12012. recommend checkpoint resumes where supported
ravi: follow-ups: 1) add canary gate for nat-scaling changes; 2) add autoscaler predicate to ignore nodes with active gpu-anchored pods; 3) MON ticket for conntrack usage alert
maya: recap: cause = nat endpoint scale-down -> conntrack saturation -> CNI failures -> nodes NotReady -> scheduler evictions; mitigation = nat pool scale-up + CNI restart + warmpool bump + scheduler tweak. closing while monitoring :thumbsup:
